Compute Match — Product Overview
What is Compute Match?
Compute Match, also called the Compute MatchMake System (internal project key NCPMS, code
name Clustrufﬂe), is an NVIDIA web platform that connects customers who need GPU compute
capacity with NVIDIA Cloud Providers (NCPs) who own and operate GPU infrastructure.
In one sentence: customers ﬁnd GPU clusters, send reservation requests, and NCPs accept,
negotiate, and contract those requests, while NVIDIA Platform Admins oversee the marketplace.

A single user can hold both customer and NCP access; they switch between them with Switch
proﬁle to in the account menu.
The core idea in ﬁve steps
1. NCPs publish capacity. An NCP uploads a CSV describing how many GPUs of which
platform (for example H100, B200, GB200) are available, in which country and city, and from
which date.
2. Customers search. A customer opens Find a Cluster to Reserve, ﬁlters by platform, region,
country, GPU count, tenure, and earliest start date, and sees matching clusters on a world
map and as cards.
3. Customers request. The customer submits a reservation request for one cluster, or for up to
3 clusters from different NCPs at once (multi-NCP request). If nothing ﬁts, they submit a
custom request that NVIDIA admins broker manually.
4. NCPs respond. Each selected NCP receives an email with a secure magic link. The NCP
accepts (moving the request to In Process), rejects, or counteroffers, and ﬁnally clicks
Conﬁrm Contract.
5. Contract. The ﬁrst NCP to contract wins; the other NCPs’ offerings on the same request are
cancelled as superseded. Capacity is allocated, and the deal is synced to Salesforce as an
Offtake record.

Unserviceable

status

the NPN portal) to join as an NCP
Important timers (defaults)
An NCP has 7 days to accept a request routed to them (acceptance window).
After accepting, the NCP and customer have 45 days to reach a contract (contract negotiation
window).
Reminder emails are sent 3 days before each deadline.
A magic link is valid for 1 hour, and can be regenerated for up to 7 days after routing.
Custom requests never expire automatically.
Platform Admins can extend either window by 1 to 200 days.
Technology at a glance
Frontend: Next.js 15, React 19, Ant Design 6, Tailwind CSS 4, NextAuth 5 with Keycloak.
Backend: Python 3.13, FastAPI, Domain-Driven Design with hexagonal architecture,
SQLAlchemy, PostgreSQL, Alembic migrations.
Workﬂows: Temporal (Temporal Cloud in shared environments) with a Python workﬂow
worker.
Identity: Keycloak with NVIDIA Starﬂeet SSO, custom Keycloak extensions.
Analytics: Apache Superset dashboards.
Platform: Google Cloud — GKE Autopilot, Cloud SQL PostgreSQL, Memorystore Redis,
Secret Manager; deployed with Terraform and Helm through GitLab CI.
Integrations: Salesforce (Offtake sync and partner-domain sync), email notiﬁcations.
Where to get help
In the app: Page Help (the ?  icon) for context help and User Manual (book icon) for the full
role-ﬁltered manual.
Support email for access problems: computematchmake@nvidia.com.
Developer docs: the docs/  folder in the repository, also published as the Compute Match
documentation site.
